Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

BUILT DIFFERENT

We believe there's a better way to build. One that moves faster, thinks bigger, and gives people the ownership to challenge what's been done before. We're not here to follow the standard. We're here to set a new one. We don't believe the best work happens inside rigid boxes. People are given real ownership, real responsibility, and the space to operate beyond a title. Scope grows with impact. Responsibility grows with trust. And the people who step up help shape what comes next. We're building an organization around ownership, not hierarchy, where your influence is defined by what you take on, not what's written on your email signature.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Hut 8 is seeking a Pre-Construction Summer Intern to support the development of next-generation digital infrastructure. This role will work directly with the pre-construction and development team on active data center projects during the early phases of development.

This position offers direct exposure to the development of large-scale data center and energy infrastructure, providing hands-on experience with how projects move from site control and permitting through engineering and pre-construction readiness.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

+   Track permitting, entitlement, and regulatory milestones, including dependencies and potential risks to project timelines

+   Support coordination with local jurisdictions, utilities, engineering consultants, and construction partners

+   Assist with development budget tracking, cost reporting, and variance monitoring across project phases

+   Maintain project schedules, milestone trackers, and internal dashboards used to monitor development progress

+   Support documentation and coordination of power, fiber, and other critical infrastructure planning

+   Prepare structured summaries and briefing materials for internal leadership updates

+   Organize and maintain project documentation, development trackers, and internal data repositories

+   Assist the development team with ad hoc analysis and project execution support as projects advance through pre-construction

+   Overall site due diligence & Feasibility – reviewing initial reports to determine if the land is susceptible to development 

+   Engineering & Design coordination 

+   Due Diligence cost and vendor bid analysis 

+   Site planning & site logistics

WHAT YOU BRING

+  Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s program in Engineering, Construction Management, Real Estate Development, Finance, Economics, or a related field

+  Graduating in December 2027 or June 2028 with an undergraduate or graduate degree

+  Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.3

+  Experience working with structured data, spreadsheets, trackers, or project documentation

+  Interest in infrastructure development, energy systems, or data center development

+  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a high level of attention to detail

+  Proficient in reading and interpreting construction drawings, plans, and product specifications

+  Track record of personal accountability, integrity, and respect for others, the company, and oneself

+  Exceptional interpersonal skills to support team cohesion and successful project execution

+  Strong written and verbal communication skills for working with diverse groups and individuals

+  Comfortable working in fast-paced environments with shifting priorities and multiple deadlines, while contributing to inclusive and cooperative teams

+  Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook

BUILT FOR THIS

If you are mission-driven, ownership-minded, drawn to hard problems, willing to challenge convention, and ready to build the playbook.

If you aren’t waiting for every answer, looking for layers of approval, leading from a distance, attached to “the way it’s always been done,” or looking for just another role.

Asher Genoot, Architect

  • Experience selling to law-enforcement, central-government, financial-intelligence, tax, regulatory, or cyber organizations.

  • A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively with technical, services, product, and customer teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in financial intelligence, investigations, cyber security, AML, digital assets, blockchain analytics, or cryptocurrency.

  • Additional languages relevant to the territory.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

You belong here.

With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Solutions Consultant, Post-Sales at Ramp partner with Account Management to deepen and expand relationships with existing Ramp customers. You'll act as the technical and financial subject matter expert across the customer lifecycle — running product demonstrations to expand customers onto new Ramp products, while bringing the depth needed to resolve complex ERP integrations, configuration challenges, and technical blockers.

 

You'll collaborate closely with Account Managers to assess requirements, design scalable solutions, and ensure fast time-to-value as customers grow with Ramp. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers. This role requires strong technical skills — comfort with APIs, ERP systems, and integration architecture — paired with the communication ability to translate complexity into clear business value for finance and operations stakeholders.

 

This role is specifically focused on Strategic Enterprise customers, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with Account Managers to demonstrate new Ramp products and features to existing customers, building the business case for expansion through customized demos and workflow illustrations

  • Evaluate customer requirements for expansion opportunities, assessing fit through use-case analysis, ROI assessments, and technical scoping

  • Design and recommend best-fit Ramp architecture — including when and how to use APIs, ERP integrations, and HRIS connectors — based on each customer's existing systems and workflows

  • Act as a technical advisor to customers and internal teams, guiding integration, configuration, and system design decisions without writing code directly

  • Troubleshoot ERP and integration blockers, and guide customers through complex configuration decisions across NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion, and others

  • Support Account Managers on technical workstreams, ensuring faster time-to-value during product rollouts and expansions

  • Be a subject matter expert across accounting systems and integration partners; advocate for integration development in line with customer needs alongside Product and Partners

  • Influence Ramp's product roadmap by channeling customer pain points and feedback to Product and Engineering teams

  • Contribute to internal documentation, tooling, and knowledge bases that scale Ramp's ability to support integration use cases across a growing customer base

What You Need

  • 4+ years in Solutions Consulting, Technical Consulting, Implementation, or a similar customer-facing technical role in SaaS or fintech

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, finance, business, or a related field

  • Hands-on familiarity with ERP systems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle Fusion) and finance/accounting workflows

  • Comfort with APIs, integration logic, and system architecture — and the ability to explain those concepts clearly to finance and operations stakeholders

  • Experience running product demonstrations and translating complex technical capabilities into clear business value

  • Strong communication skills: able to guide customers toward scalable approaches and diplomatically steer conversations when requests are misaligned with product capabilities or best practices

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program.

Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner.

This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done.

 

The opportunity

  • Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise

  • Map the acquired company's existing controls to Payward's control framework, and identify gaps against the external frameworks the entity falls under once in scope

  • Score control maturity at the entity level and document the basis for each score

  • Define remediation milestones that are achievable for the acquired team's size and maturity, sequenced by risk reduction rather than by framework order

  • Track milestones to closure and report status to Security GRC leadership and the M&A Technology Team

  • Recommend the endpoint for each entity: full migration onto Payward platforms, or uplift to a maturity level the central program can absorb

  • Load acquired-entity risks into the enterprise risk register and keep them current

  • Prepare acquired entities for inclusion in external audit scope, including evidence collection and walkthrough support

  • Act as the Security GRC point of contact for acquired-entity leadership, finance, and internal audit

  • Maintain policy coverage for acquired entities, including building entity-specific policy libraries where the parent policy set does not apply cleanly

  • Feed recurring findings back into the diligence process, so later deals are assessed against known patterns

  • Document the onboarding process so that it is repeatable and not dependent on one person

 

What Will you Do

  • Target Assessment

    • Review target security posture during diligence: control environment, identity and access management, infrastructure, third-party dependencies, and prior audit or examination history

    • Produce a written assessment of each target against the Payward security baseline, separating the risks that matter to the deal from those that matter to steady-state operations

    • Give the M&A Technology Team and deal sponsors a clear read on what integration will cost in control remediation terms

  • Control Mapping and Framework Onboarding

    • Map acquired controls to Payward's framework and to the external frameworks the entity becomes subject to

    • Identify which parent-company controls extend to the entity as they are, which need an entity-specific variant, and which have no equivalent at all

    • Build the entity's policy library where the parent policy set does not cover it

  • Remediation and Milestones

    • Set milestones the acquired team can meet, each with a date, an owner, and a stated risk reduction

    • Sequence work so that the highest-risk gaps close first rather than the easiest ones

    • Run the cadence for tracking remediation and escalating overdue or material risks Prepare proposed risk acceptances, including the rationale and compensating controls, and present them to leadership for decision

  • Program Integration

    • Prepare entities for external audit inclusion and support fieldwork

    • Keep acquired-entity risk visible in the enterprise risk register and in Security GRC reporting

    • Hand each entity over to central GRC coverage once its maturity supports it, with the handover documented

    • Integrate 3rd parties and vendors into Payward

What you bring

  • 5-7+ years in security governance, IT risk, or compliance, including regulated financial services, fintech, or virtual asset environments

  • Direct experience onboarding an acquired company into an existing controls or compliance program. This is the core of the role

  • Working knowledge of SOX/ICFR IT general controls and what external auditors accept as evidence

  • Experience with at least two of ISO 27001, SOC 1, SOC 2, and PCI DSS, including mapping controls across frameworks

  • Ability to assess control maturity and set remediation plans the receiving team completes, including teams below Payward's maturity level

  • Hands-on delivery: you write the scope, collect the evidence, and close gaps yourself when needed

  • Sound judgment on priorities with incomplete information, and the sense to escalate decisions that need leadership

  • Ability to build working relationships with control owners in IAM, infrastructure, and engineering

  • Ability to translate control gaps into risk language that deal teams and executives can act on

  • Strong project management across cross-functional, distributed teams

  • Preferred

    • CISA, CRISC, CISM, CISSP, or ISO 27001 Lead Implementer

    • M&A or post-merger technology integration experience

    • Familiarity with PKM

 

Why This Role

  • You will own a domain end to end rather than supporting someone else's. There is no incumbent process and no one else doing this work today

  • Acquisitions are one of the fastest-moving parts of the business, and security integration sits on the critical path for each one

  • You will work directly with deal teams, acquired-company leadership, external auditors, and Security GRC leadership, with visibility into how acquisitions are evaluated and closed

  • Payward is preparing for public company reporting, which means the controls you put in place at acquired entities are the ones external auditors will test

  • The scope of this role grows with the acquisition pipeline, across jurisdictions and regulatory regimes

  • You will join a remote-first, international team

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Risk Partnerships team is an essential part of Stripe’s Global Partnerships organization. Our team is responsible for building and maintaining relationships with key partner banks to manage risk for Stripe’s business activities. These banking partnerships enable Stripe to accept and make payments, provide credit, move and store money, and develop new products and solutions to meet our users’ needs. We work across a broad range of risk and compliance topics, including credit, fraud, regulatory, financial crime, reputational, product, and operational risks.

What you’ll do

You’ll work with key banking and network partners across North America that provide bank identification number (BIN) sponsorship for merchant acquiring and card issuing. You’ll also bring experience managing risk across money transmission.

Risk management is a critical part of these relationships, and you’ll need a broad understanding of risk disciplines across merchant acquiring and banking. You’ll lead activities to improve risk management interactions between Stripe and its partners, manage key aspects of partner relationships, and execute high-impact initiatives.

You’ll work closely with internal and external stakeholders to set objectives, coordinate priorities, and drive execution. Internally, you’ll coordinate with product and engineering teams, as well as Risk, Fraud, Financial Crime & Supportability, Operations, Legal, and Finance. Externally, you’ll work closely with partners’ risk and compliance teams, including senior management.

Responsibilities

  • Lead risk-focused initiatives with global financial partners, including banks, networks, and payment methods, to support new business opportunities and user verticals, develop shared risk methodologies, and establish and maintain compliance with agreed risk appetites
  • Manage relationships with key risk counterparts at partner banks and develop projects and initiatives that support those relationships
  • Deliver business and policy recommendations that inform Stripe’s risk posture
  • Represent and negotiate Stripe’s risk approach with banking partners
  • Improve existing partner-facing risk management capabilities and develop new ones
  • Lead risk-related partnership and product discussions with banking partners to align on risk approaches and strategies
  • Identify and pursue business opportunities by creating risk-aware solutions that expand Stripe’s product and user base through banking partnerships

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in a risk-related role at a bank or merchant acquirer, or a role requiring deep knowledge of risk and compliance issues; 5+ years of experience in risk management at a bank or merchant acquirer
  • Ability to represent Stripe on risk, compliance, and product issues with banking partners to maintain positive relationships
  • Strong organizational, planning, and written and verbal communication skills to support understanding, collaboration, and issue resolution
  • 2+ years of experience improving processes and scaling solutions
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, including handling difficult situations, negotiating timelines, and influencing stakeholders across organizations and borders, along with the ability to work proactively and independently in uncertain and ambiguous environments

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with financial crime programs, including know your customer and know your business processes, anti-money laundering, sanctions, and counter-terrorist financing, with practical knowledge of the Bank Secrecy Act and anti-money laundering regulations
  • Strong understanding of the complex risks involved in managing a merchant acquiring business, including high-risk sectors
  • Market experience across America and Canada, with an understanding of how current and future regulations will affect Stripe and its banking partners
  • Experience using technology to develop and embed scalable risk and operational processes
descriptions.job-06dinfw:
Hut 8 brings exceptional people together to solve the world’s most consequential problems at the intersection of energy and technology. Today, that means building infrastructure for AI at a pace and scale without precedent. Tomorrow, it could mean powering a new era of innovation through robotics, advanced manufacturing, or an industry that does not yet exist. Whatever the technology demands, our ambition holds: to build the defining physical infrastructure company of our generation.

We look for thinkers and builders with the rigor, humility, and ownership to solve problems at this scale. They start from zero and choose truth over tradition. They back the best idea, whatever its source. They bet on themselves and embrace the hard truths that force them to grow. Our commitment is to keep the path from idea to execution short, trust them with critical decisions and the work that follows, and surround them with colleagues whose curiosity extends beyond their expertise.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Field Manager, CXQC, Principal to support the testing, verification, and turnover of critical infrastructure systems across our data center and mission-critical facility portfolio. This is a hands-on, field-oriented role responsible for executing commissioning programs from pre-functional testing through integrated system verification. The role is project-based, which means assignment locations will vary — candidates must be comfortable with travel and potential relocation to support active project sites across our growing footprint.

Some of the key responsibilities you should expect are the following:

  • Execute pre-functional, functional, and integrated system commissioning activities across mechanical, electrical, and controls systems
  • Support startup and commissioning of critical infrastructure including UPS systems, generators, switchgear, PDUs, CRAC/CRAH units, chillers, and BMS/EPMS platforms
  • Document commissioning activities, test results, deficiencies, and resolutions in accordance with project commissioning plans
  • Coordinate closely with general contractors, subcontractors, equipment vendors, and the owner's engineering team to sequence and execute commissioning activities
  • Conduct site observations to verify installations are complete and compliant with design drawings and specifications prior to testing
  • Identify field deficiencies and work with the project team to drive timely resolution before milestone dates
  • Support and ensure readiness for operational turnover
  • Maintain accurate, detailed commissioning records including test reports, punch lists, and equipment start-up logs
  • Enforce safety protocols and ensure compliance with site-specific safety plans and OSHA standards during all commissioning activities
  • Communicate daily progress, issues, and schedule risks to the appropriate project stakeholders

ABOUT YOU

  • 2–5 years of hands-on experience in commissioning, startup, or field engineering within data centers, mission-critical facilities, or large-scale infrastructure projects
  • Working knowledge of mechanical, electrical, and controls systems common to mission-critical environments (UPS, generators, switchgear, cooling, BMS/EPMS)
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, single-line diagrams, and equipment submittals
  • Strong understanding of commissioning documentation requirements including test scripts, punch lists, and turnover packages
  • Experience coordinating with multiple trades and subcontractors on active construction sites
  • Comfortable operating in fast-paced, milestone-driven project environments with shifting priorities
  • Detail-oriented with strong written and verbal communication skills — able to produce clear field reports and communicate issues effectively to project stakeholder
  • Willingness and ability to travel to project sites; relocation may be required based on project assignment
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification preferred
  • Experience with mission-critical infrastructure commissioning (power, cooling, fiber, telecom) is a strong plus
  • Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license; active passport preferred for potential international project assignments

ABOUT THE WORK ENVIRONMENT

This role is project-based and will be assigned to active data center construction and commissioning sites within Hut 8's portfolio. Assignment locations will vary and candidates should expect regular travel with the possibility of extended on-site presence or relocation depending on project needs. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

About the Company

Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

You will have the opportunity to deliver massive impact at a hypergrowth company backed by some of the top investors in fintech, crypto, and SaaS. In January 2026, we closed a $250M Series C led by ICONIQ, valuing Rain at $1.95B, with Sapphire Ventures, Norwest, Galaxy Ventures, Dragonfly, Bessemer Venture Partners, FirstMark, Lightspeed, and Endeavor Catalyst also participating. If you're curious, bold, and excited to help shape a borderless financial future, we'd love to talk.

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About the Team

Rain is organizing a national trust bank to bring regulated custody, reserve management, and stablecoin issuance inside the same group, and we need one person whose job is keeping that effort on schedule. You'll work with the proposed bank's CEO, our regulatory lead, outside advisors, and our product and people teams, and you'll own the program plan, the tracker, the calendar, and the document record for everything that has to happen before the bank opens.

This is a coordination role with a project-management backbone, reporting to our Head of Regulatory Strategy. You won't make legal, regulatory, hiring, or product decisions. You'll make sure they get made on time, that the people making them have what they need, and that nothing is lost, duplicated, or late. The role is new; you'll build its systems from day one.

What you’ll do

  • Own one program plan across every workstream: milestones, owners, dependencies, dates. Update it daily by checking with owners, not waiting for them.

  • Run the meeting cadence: weekly status and workstream check-ins, with agendas and materials sent ahead and action items sent the same day.

  • Log, file, and distribute regulator correspondence the day it arrives; break it into items with owners and internal due dates; assemble and format the responses; keep the record of what was sent and when.

  • Consolidate existing trackers and document lists into one library and one request log, then keep both current.

  • Run down documents from across the company: find who has it, task them with a date, follow up until it arrives, file it.

  • Enforce document standards on everything outbound: formatting, numbering, defined terms, cross-references, file names. Convert, assemble, or package documents when someone needs it done.

  • Coordinate recruiting logistics with HR and search firms: scheduling, feedback, offer paperwork, and the regulatory filings each hire requires.

  • Engage and schedule consultants for interview preparation and policy drafting; track deliverables.

  • Keep the inventory of policies, procedures, charters, and agreements that must be in place before opening, with owner, reviewer, and date for each.

  • Flag slippage before it happens, with the date and the reason.

You are likely to succeed if you have:

  • 3+ years coordinating multi-party projects with hard external deadlines, in a law firm, financial institution, regulator, consulting firm, or similar.

  • A record of running your own work without supervision. You send the reminders; you don't need them.

  • Advanced Word (styles, numbering, cross-references, tracked changes) and Excel; comfortable building a tracker others rely on.

  • Precise, brief written communication.

  • Demonstrated attention to detail. We'll ask for examples.

  • Discretion. The work is confidential and you'll sign an NDA before seeing any of it.

  • Authorization to work in the United States and ability to pass a background check.

Bonus attributes:

  • Experience supporting a bank regulatory filing, examination, or application.

  • Experience coordinating executive recruiting or board onboarding.

  • A legal, compliance, or executive operations coordinator background.

  • Familiarity with digital asset custody or payments.

Things that enable a fulfilling, healthy and happy experience at Rain:

Flexible time off 🌴 Unlimited vacation can be daunting, so we require Rainmakers to take 10 days minimum for themselves.

Flexible working ☕ We support a flexible workplace – work from home, come into an office, or both. We want everyone to work in an environment where they're their most confident and productive selves. New Rainmakers receive a stipend to set up a comfortable home workspace.

Easy to access benefits 🧠 For US Rainmakers, we cover 95% of your health, dental, and vision plan costs and 90% for your dependents, plus a 100% company-subsidized life insurance plan.

Retirement goals💡 Plan for the future with confidence. We offer a 401(k) with a 4% company match.

Equity plan 📦 Every Rainmaker gets an equity option plan so we all benefit from our success.

Health and Wellness 📚 High performance begins from within. Rainmakers receive a monthly stipend to be used for eligible health and wellness spending like gym memberships/fitness classes, massages, acupuncture - whatever recharges you!

In-office meals 🍜 Rainmakers working from the office enjoy lunch and dinner on us, covered with a DoorDash credit.

Team summits ✨ Summits play an important role at Rain. Time together helps us build relationships and a common destiny. Expect team and company offsites, both domestic and international.

About HIFI

HIFI is a stablecoin infrastructure company building technology for the next-generation of financial products. We build tools for payments and tokenized money products across money movement, cards, and capital markets. Institutions and enterprises already use our platform and APIs to move billions of dollars in production environments around the world, and we are still early.

 

Founded in 2022, our organization is flat and our team is talent dense. We work in person at our office in Flatiron and are intentional about who we work with. We've raised $37 million from world-class investors, including a Series A led by Left Lane Capital.

 

About the Team

HIFI's engineering team builds the payments infrastructure that fintechs and financial institutions use to move money on stablecoin rails. The team owns the APIs, ledger, and on-chain systems behind every payment HIFI processes, and works closely with product and compliance to make sure that infrastructure is reliable, secure, and ready for regulated use. As HIFI's volume grows and more institutions build on our platform, this team will decide how stablecoin payments hold up at the scale and standard that traditional financial infrastructure is held to.

 

As a Security Engineer at HIFI you will help own the security of our company and the infrastructure behind our payments products day to day. You'll build HIFI's security program from the ground up, including identity and access management, endpoint security, and the cloud and network controls that protect our systems and data. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you'll set the security roadmap based on risk, put core capabilities like monitoring, incident response, and secrets management in place, and write the policies that govern how HIFI handles access and information. You'll also be the person the team relies on to keep HIFI ready for audits and partner security reviews as we expand into more regulated markets.

 

What you will build

  • Design and implement the HIFI security roadmap from first principles to production, prioritizing by risk.

  • Lead threat modeling and hardening for our money movement systems.

  • Build core security capabilities, including monitoring and detection, incident response, secrets management, API security, and CI/CD hardening.

  • Own cloud and network security architecture, including segmentation, encryption, and least-privilege access.

  • Own endpoint and identity security across our devices and SaaS tools.

  • Reinforce engineering best practices around secure development and infrastructure.

  • Write and maintain information security policies and procedures.

  • Ensure HIFI meets information security compliance and audit expectations as we scale to more regulated markets.

  • Collaborate with engineering, product, compliance, and leadership to move fast without compromising safety.

 

You might be a fit if

  • 6+ years of experience in security engineering.

  • Deep, hands-on AWS and network security experience, with infrastructure managed in Terraform.

  • Experience owning security controls in a regulated environment, such as payments or financial services.

  • Strong web application and API security skills, including modern authentication and authorization.

  • Experience writing audit-ready policies and procedures.

  • Experience building security practices from the ground up in a fast-paced startup.

  • Comfort writing and debugging backend code, ideally JavaScript/TypeScript.

  • Hands-on experience with SIEM, MDM, and database security, especially Postgres.

  • A builder's mindset: you ship practical fixes quickly and know when good enough is safe enough.

  • Interest in stablecoins and their potential to change how money moves around the world.

 

Why This Role Matters

HIFI moves billions of dollars for banks and fintechs, and keeping that money safe depends on the security of everything behind it, from our cloud infrastructure to the laptops our team works on. This is a chance to build HIFI's security program from its foundation and make safety a default part of how the company operates as it grows.
